title: NATIVE ON build, Agent 5 uploads, u0/u1 x5 version (Agent 1 05:31): u0 batch-2 defaults vs u1 legacy upload CPU paths; 5 runs each with 60 s windows, load phase scored by bench/agent5/load_phase.py. Title/attract loop from boot, no input needed
notes: U0/U1 X5 VERSION (Agent 1, 05:31; Agent 5, after task #20): the two-arm cut of bench/agent5/matrix-native-uploads-45.json (sha256 114A0242..., unchanged, still the three-arm option). Same bin, cvars, env, timings, 60 s window floor and sys.csv; the u0 and u1 arms are byte-identical to its arms. u2 (staging pool) is left out: it is expected to tie u0, and its checks are functional (Agent 8's s2 row passed them). Not scheduled: Agent 1 decides if and when it runs (user window, quiet machine).

WHY: Agent 8's s-rows (04:38-04:51, build/agent8/matrix/20261122-0438; n = 1 each, hidden desktop, slow-op logging on, no sys.csv) had s1 (u1 plus slow-op logging) worse than s0 in the 60-180 s window: fps 94.6 vs 109, p99 42.3 vs 23.9 ms, 241 vs 30 frames over 33 ms (s2 tied s0: 110 fps, 23.3 ms, 27). In the first 30 s, s1's max frame was 300 ms vs 90 ms. One run without sys.csv can't rule out the slow CPU state, so this matrix repeats u0 vs u1 five times each, interleaved, with sys.csv on.

BIN DIR: build/agent2/native3-bin (Agent 2, staged 02:45:57; exe sha256 7F7F8586D219465C, MANIFEST.txt B50FE8D4A16565DA, native GPU fingerprint 8f849b69907d4006). It is the S3 snapshot with NATIVE_GPU=ON. Batch 2 is in (all three batch-2 strings are in the exe, and MANIFEST.txt lists the 8 Agent 5 files) and so is fix-a, so it boots with the settings frontend on (Agent 8 boot PASS, build/agent8/runs/0256-native3). Do not swap in an older native bin: native-bin (S1) has no env switch, so u1 would equal u0, and native-bin and native2-bin throw at startup with the frontend on.

WINDOW (Agent 1's 60 s floor): settle_s 50 + warmup_s 10 from the first-frame signal, so the scored window covers 60-120 s after the first frame (cold run: 60-90 s). min_window_after_ff_s is set to 60 explicitly (the runner default), so no warm-up is raised. On the frame clock (interval_ms summed over the rows before frames.window.first_row), Agent 8's S3 runs started their windows 0.2-0.4 s after settle + warm-up, so expect about 60.3 s after the real first frame. The light-to-heavy title switch comes 30.6-32.6 s after the first frame (window 3 and S3 runs), so it falls in the settle, about 28 s before the window. load_phase.py prints each run's window start (ff->win s) and flags win<60s if one starts early. -Quick (settle 5 s) is functional only and never scored.

UNCAPPED (SG rule): both arms pass native_fps_limit=0 and framerate_limit=0. The runner adds the standard flags itself (common.ps1:99-100: --native_settings_load=false --discord_rpc=false --audio_mute=true --pause_when_unfocused=false), so they are not repeated here. No arm sets native_settings_frontend=false: the build must boot with the settings frontend on. With the frontend on, the cap is LEGO_NATIVE_FPS_LIMIT if that env is set, else the native_fps_limit cvar (settings_snapshot.cpp:64-65; the frontend only reads the env). No arm sets that env, so the cvar uncaps it. Check: the native_fps_limit_cvar column of native-frames.csv (the cap in force) must be 0 in every row; load_phase.py flags capN otherwise. It was 0 in every row of all 4 s-rows.

SCORING 1, the scored window (the runner, as usual): mean fps, p50, p99, over_33ms, over_100ms, max_ms and CPU over 60-120 s after the first frame. It measures the steady-state upload cost of the title/attract loop: textures streamed in after boot (u1: scalar untile and byte swap). A tie is a valid result. Report runs with Agent 8's light-phase flag or a sys.csv disturbance flag separately.

SCORING 2, the load phase (no extra runs): after the matrix, run: python bench/agent5/load_phase.py <matrix output dir> --ref u0 --md <matrix output dir>/load-phase.md --csv <matrix output dir>/load-phase.csv --json <matrix output dir>/load-phase.json. From row 0 of each run's native-frames.csv (perf.csv as a cross-check) it scores the first 60 s after the first frame: frames over 33/50/100 ms, hitch ms, max frame, p99, launch to first frame (game.log 'Native presentation: frame=0'), first frame to title (the draw-count switch), title max (max frame from 2 s before to 5 s after the switch) and o20 5s+ (frames over 20 ms after 5 s, a busy-machine check). It compares u1 with u0 (difference of medians and an exact permutation p) and leaves out cold, light-phase, failed and short runs. Stdlib Python, one thread, read-only on the run dirs. These are first-use costs, not timing results.

EXPECT. u0, from the 5 quiet window-3 n0 runs (native2-bin, frontend off; native3-bin with the frontend on may shift the absolute values): o33 3-4, o50 0-2, o100 0-1, max 50-154 ms, all in the startup burst in the first 1.4 s (per-run PSO compiles and first uploads); p99 10-12 ms; title max 13-16 ms; first frame to title 30.6-31.2 s; launch to first frame 12.7-17.2 s. u1 (old CPU paths, same output bytes): a bigger startup burst (s1: max 300 ms vs 90 ms) and maybe a spike at the title switch. Scored window: if s1's single-run deficit is real, u1 is worse in all 5 runs (lower fps, higher p99 and over-33 ms counts; exact p 0.008 at 5v5); if it came from the slow CPU state, a tie, which is also valid. The load phase separates u1 from u0 only if the effect is large and consistent, for example 2 or more extra frames over 33 ms, or a title max above 20 ms, in every run. First frame to title should not move: it follows a timed intro.
Neither arm may log 'Native texture staging pool' lines: only u2 (not in this matrix) enables the pool.

CORRUPTION (nobody watches the screen): u1 runs the old upload CPU paths, which must produce the same bytes as u0; a wrong untile or byte swap would draw wrong textures without any log line, so only a person or a screenshot can rule it out. Log checks per run (game*.log); each count must be 0, or the same in u1 as in u0: 'texture upload allocation failed' (textures.cpp:2446), 'texture allocation failed' (textures.cpp:1107), 'failed to allocate' (buffers.cpp:467), 'cannot wait for submission after device removal' (device.cpp:657), and 'Native texture binding:' / 'Native texture binding totals:' (draw.cpp:928/932, with unavailable, upload_rejected and view_lost counts). Baseline: 0 [error] lines and 31 non-INSTALL [warning] lines in window-3 0030-n0-r1, build/agent8/runs/0256-native3 and all 4 s-rows. If u1 differs from u0 in any of them, stop the arm and tell Agent 5.
No LEGO_NATIVE_TIMING, LEGO_NATIVE_SLOW_OPERATIONS or debug layer in these arms.

QUIET MACHINE: the load phase is very sensitive to background load. Busy runs (verify3b, and S3 n1-n3 on the hidden desktop) had 27-88 frames over 33 ms and 112-295 frames over 20 ms after 5 s, and the 0256 boot run (94% system busy) had 44 over 20 ms, against 3-4 and 0-2 on the quiet window-3 runs. Run it on an idle machine; load_phase.py flags a run with more than 20 frames over 20 ms after 5 s as noisy. sys_csv is on, as in window 4's matrix: every run logs sys.csv and sys.json (1 s), so input, foreground loss, screensaver and power changes get flagged.

SIZE: 11 runs, 1 unscored cold u0 and then 5 rounds of u0 and u1. -PlanOnly: about 28 min; at the S3 overheads (launch to first frame 13-21 s against the planner's 12 s, close + cooldown 21 s against 20 s) expect up to about 2 min more. If the window is shorter, -Repeats 4 is 9 runs, about 23 min (smallest exact p 0.029).

arms.note: Agent 5 u0: batch-2 defaults (SIMD untile, no staging zero-fill, SIMD byte swap, no staging pool)
Agent 5 u1: old upload CPU paths. Expect slower uploads than u0 (more or longer upload spikes)
